item.title: Pope warns against new arms race
item.description: At his general audience, Pope Leo XIV appealed for renewed nuclear arms-control efforts and asked Catholics to proclaim the Gospel in ways that speak to people’s real lives.

item.title: Pope Leo’s liturgical celebrations for February, March, and Holy Week
item.description: The Vatican has published the schedule of liturgies that Pope Leo XIV will celebrate in February, March, and the beginning of April, which includes the start of Lent, Holy Week, and Easter.

item.title: Monastic-style retreat planned for pope and Roman Curia at start of Lent
item.description: Trappist Bishop Erik Varden of Trondheim will preach the week of spiritual exercises, with two daily meditations beginning Feb. 22.

item.title: American sister ends 40 years in Bangladesh forming priests, founding school
item.description: Sister Miriam Francis Perlewitz taught Scripture at Bangladesh’s national seminary for decades and co-founded an inclusive school serving Christian, Muslim, and Hindu children.

item.title: Why Slovak bishops are defending 25-year-old agreement with Holy See
item.description: A Slovak opposition party has questioned aspects of the country’s 25-year-old agreement with the Vatican, prompting Catholic bishops to defend the accord as serving the common good of all citizens.

item.title: Church fresco angel that resembled Italian prime minister painted over to end controversy
item.description: The restored fresco in an ancient church in Rome sparked controversy after one of the angels depicted in the restoration bore a striking resemblance to Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni.
